text.p: Copper closed steady, aluminium firmed and other metals closed mixed on the LME. In other commodities of Australian interest, gold and wheat prices eased, but oil firmed on technical buying. The CRB index was up 0.09 at 239.42.
METALS - Copper prices backtracked from early highs but still closed steadier on the LME, against a background of June tightness ahead of Wednesday's option declarations.

Copper prices trended higher from the outset but the market also stalled near $2,440 resistance. By the close, three months was back at $2,422, up just $4 from Friday's kerb, while the cash/threes rate was around $145.
Aluminium found the impetus to chase up and challenge the resistance stretching up to $1,600, building on the supportive buying seen on recent dips.
Although the close was just under $1,600, the charts are in better shape, and further gains should be secured if the run of stock draw-downs continues. Last trade was at $1,598, up $23 from Friday.
Nickel prices held above early 6-1/2 month lows during the afternoon, but still closed lower after confirming technical weakness under $7,000 today.
The rally from the lows reflected news that a weekend explosion at Outokumpu's Harjavalta smelter would result in 5,000 tonnes of lost production. Copper output was only briefly interrupted.
This helped the nickel market partially recover from the hit taken after the ending of a four week strike at Inco Sudbury. Last trade was at $6,860, still down $110.
Zinc continued to correct lower after earlier failing to break above a 6-3/4 year high around $1,430, and prices closed at $1,418, down $10.
Lead was lacklustre throughout, and closed at $627, down $3 from Friday. Tin was equally lifeless, and ended at $5,570, up just $10. Alloy was stable at $1,450/60 a tonne.

GOLD - Gold prices ended at a new four-an-a-quarter year low, dragging silver prices lower also, but platinum group metals ended mixed as another deadline for the resumption of Russian exports passed without any sign of metal deliveries. COMEX August gold ended down 60 cents at $335.30 an ounce, after sliding to a fresh life-of-contract low at $334.60. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $333.70/20, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $334.55 an ounce.

OIL - NYMEX crude ended firm on technical buying amid a delay in the restart of Iraqi oil sales. August crude settled 34 cents a barrel higher at $19.80 after rising as high as $19.90. Prompt crude broke technical resistance created by the session high on June 25 of $19.75. That level was the highest point for spot crude since June 6.

WHEAT - KCBT hard red winter closed sharply down after earlier slipping to its lowest level in almost three years, depressed by the continued improvement in the outlook for this year's crops. July wheat slipped to a contract low of $3.30-1/2 a bushel, the lowest level for the nearby month since July 1994. It closed of 8-1/2 cents at $3.30-3/4.
